skill.name: x402socks
skill.description: Review paid x402socks proxy access for authorized HTTPS requests. The skill documents USDC payments on Base, token management, and TLS HTTP CONNECT.
skill.summary: Compare proxy packages, review payment terms, and diagnose token status.
skill.author: x402socks

security_audit.summary: Most matches are documentation syntax, ordinary shell operations, or expected use of provider APIs. The review found weak payment approval verification, incomplete traffic controls, and paths that expose credentials or untrusted text. No evidence was found of bundled malware or deliberate credential theft.

remediation.issue: Approval records do not prove human consent.
remediation.suggestion: Verify a signed or broker-issued approval outside the agent's write scope. Persist one-use and settlement state in the same trusted service.

remediation.issue: Example clients do not fully enforce proxy routing or destination policy.
remediation.suggestion: Require a valid proxy configuration before connecting. Clear ambient bypass settings and enforce destinations at the network boundary, including every redirect.

remediation.issue: Proxy configuration can expose a reusable token through standard output.
remediation.suggestion: Replace the secret-bearing output command with a client that consumes credentials internally. Keep signing and token storage outside the agent transcript.

remediation.issue: Generic validation errors are classified as missing credentials.
remediation.suggestion: Require definitive provider-specific invalidation evidence. Treat ambiguous responses as inconclusive and check settlement records before purchasing again.

remediation.issue: Provider text reaches payment decisions and diagnostics.
remediation.suggestion: Use fixed diagnostics and validate display fields by type and meaning. Apply trusted origin checks to public discovery calls as well.

remediation.issue: Recovery examples omit the required consent check.
remediation.suggestion: Use one consent policy for recovery and enforce it before requesting a wallet signature. Update the troubleshooting table and signing examples.

semantic_findings.title: Payment approval is not authenticated
semantic_findings.description: The payment examples trust a file selected by the environment. Its unkeyed hash checks consistency, not whether a human approved the record. One-use markers prevent reuse of an ID but cannot verify authorization.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Both examples recompute a plain hash of the same file they trust. Neither verifies an independent approval signature or consults a trusted approval service.

semantic_findings.title: Curl recipes can fall back to direct traffic
semantic_findings.description: The curl recipes start the client before confirming that the helper supplied a proxy configuration. They do not disable ambient proxy bypass settings. An authorized target could receive the operator's source IP directly.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The pipe has no success gate before curl runs. Ignoring curl configuration files does not clear proxy environment settings.

semantic_findings.title: Browser allowlist cannot guarantee redirect containment
semantic_findings.description: The Playwright route handler checks the first request in a redirect chain. The final URL check happens after navigation and cannot prevent contact with an unapproved host.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Playwright routing invokes the handler only for the first request in a redirect chain. The example verifies the resulting URL only after the browser loads it.

semantic_findings.title: Generic HTTP errors can permit a new purchase
semantic_findings.description: Reconciliation treats several HTTP error statuses as definitive proof that no valid token exists. A generic gateway error can therefore permit a purchase without confirming the token state.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The helper discards the response body and assigns the same result to generic 403 and 404 responses. The payment example proceeds on that result.

semantic_findings.title: Provider error keys enter agent output unchecked
semantic_findings.description: The missing-token error prints provider-controlled field names without the usual text validation or untrusted-data label. Those names can contain misleading instructions or terminal control characters.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The error joins raw JSON keys directly into its diagnostic. No embedded instruction attempting to override this audit was found in the reviewed source.

semantic_findings.title: Recovery consent guidance conflicts
semantic_findings.description: The approval template requires a fresh decision for token recovery. The troubleshooting table directs agents to recover after a provisioning error without repeating that approval requirement.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The detailed policy requires fresh consent, but the short recovery recipes do not enforce it. Recovery issues a replacement credential and requires a wallet signature.

content.user_title: Review Paid Proxy Access with x402socks
content.value_statement: Paid proxy access requires current prices, clear authorization, and careful token handling. This skill provides quote checks, token diagnostics, and TLS proxy configuration for authorized HTTPS requests.
actual_capabilities: Lists provider packages, prices, and exit health.
Reads a live x402 payment challenge and checks its amount against a supplied cap.
Documents how to compare payment terms and a signer with an approval record.
Checks token validity, account status, and usage through provider endpoints.
Stores replacement tokens locally after rotation or signed recovery.
Produces TLS HTTP CONNECT configuration and compares proxied egress with a supplied or explicitly requested baseline.
limitations: Purchases require a compatible signer and USDC on Base.
The shell helper can quote but cannot sign purchases.
Prices, exit availability, quotas, and session limits can change.
Client examples do not guarantee that every request stays within the destination allowlist or uses the proxy.

use_cases.title: Compare packages
use_cases.description: Review package prices, quotas, and session limits without signing a payment.

use_cases.title: Plan regional staging checks
use_cases.description: Compare the reported health of regional exits for a staging service your team owns.

use_cases.title: Review a payment approval
use_cases.description: Compare a supplied quote with approved wallet, recipient, amount, and package details before signing.

prompt_templates.title: Summarize a catalog
prompt_templates.prompt: Summarize the prices, quotas, and session limits in this catalog. Do not buy or sign anything.

prompt_templates.title: Explain token status
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain this redacted token status. Separate an invalid token from an inconclusive check. Do not request my token.

prompt_templates.title: Compare a quote with approval
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare this quote with the attached approval. Check the amount, asset, recipient, package, request URL, and paying wallet. Do not sign.

prompt_templates.title: Review staging egress controls
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the proxy client configuration for our staging service. Check how it handles unavailable proxy settings and redirects. Do not send network requests.

output_examples.output: The first entry allows one session and lists a lower quota. The second allows concurrent sessions. No payment was made.

output_examples.input: Does this quote match the approved terms?
output_examples.output: The amount matches, but the recipient differs. Do not sign. Ask the approver to review the updated quote.

output_examples.input: What does this inconclusive validation result mean?
output_examples.output: The check did not establish whether the token is valid. Check the account and any settlement record before considering another payment.

best_practices: Verify the current price and exact terms with an independent approver before signing.
Keep tokens and signing credentials out of transcripts, arguments, and shared storage.
Enforce the destination allowlist at the network boundary and stop when the proxy is unavailable.
anti_patterns: Using rotating egress to evade access rules or rate limits.
Treating a timeout or ambiguous token status as permission to pay again.
Printing or pasting a live token or full proxy configuration.

faq.question: Can I inspect a quote without paying?
faq.answer: Yes. The quote helper reads the payment challenge and checks the cap. It does not sign a payment.

faq.question: Which wallet does a purchase require?
faq.answer: Use an EVM-compatible wallet funded with USDC on Base and a compatible signer.

faq.question: Does the helper use SOCKS5?
faq.answer: No. The helper uses TLS HTTP CONNECT, despite the skill name.

faq.question: Where does the helper store a token?
faq.answer: It uses a private local token file by default. It also supports a token supplied through the environment.

faq.question: Does a proxy authorize access to a destination?
faq.answer: No. Use it only for destinations that explicitly permit your access and your type of automation.

faq.question: What should I do if payment settled but provisioning failed?
faq.answer: Do not pay again. Check settlement and account status. Review the documented recovery process with the paying wallet owner.
